# wallix-bastion_domain_account_credential (Data Source)

Get information on a credential resource for a domain account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Get information about a specific domain account credential
data "wallix-bastion_domain_account" "admin" {
  domain_id    = wallix-bastion_domain.corporate.id
  account_name = "administrator"
}

data "wallix-bastion_domain_account_credential" "admin_ssh_key" {
  domain_id  = data.wallix-bastion_domain_account.admin.domain_id
  account_id = data.wallix-bastion_domain_account.admin.id
  type       = "ssh_key"
}

# Only public metadata is available; use the public key to verify configuration
output "admin_ssh_key_public" {
  value = {
    type                         = data.wallix-bastion_domain_account_credential.admin_ssh_key.type
    public_key                   = data.wallix-bastion_domain_account_credential.admin_ssh_key.public_key
    propagate_credential_change  = data.wallix-bastion_domain_account_credential.admin_ssh_key.propagate_credential_change
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account_id` (String)
- `domain_id` (String)
- `type` (String)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `passphrase` (String, Sensitive)
- `password` (String, Sensitive)
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive)
- `propagate_credential_change` (Boolean)
- `public_key` (String)

## Usage Notes

### Lookup Keys

This data source requires three keys to locate the credential:

- **domain_id**: The internal ID of the parent domain (`wallix-bastion_domain`)
- **account_id**: The internal ID of the account (the `id` attribute of `wallix-bastion_domain_account`, not its `account_name`)
- **type**: The credential type to look up, `"password"` or `"ssh_key"`

### Secret Values Are Never Returned

The Bastion API never returns secret material on read. Even though `password`, `private_key`, and `passphrase` are declared as `Computed`/`Sensitive` attributes in the schema, they will always read back as empty strings through this data source. Only non-secret metadata is actually populated:

- **type**: The credential type
- **public_key**: The public key (for `ssh_key` credentials), when previously set

Do not rely on this data source to retrieve secrets for use elsewhere in your configuration; it can only confirm that a credential of a given type exists and expose its public key. Note that `propagate_credential_change` is exposed by the schema but, like the secret fields, is only meaningfully populated by the underlying resource, not by this read-only lookup.
